data.title: Build Neon: The Glowing Sign Element
data.description: Discover how protons, neutrons, and electrons come together to form neon, the element behind bright city lights.

challenges.instruction: Place 10 protons into the nucleus to discover neon, the gas used in glowing advertising signs.
challenges.hint: Neon is element number 10 on the periodic table.
challenges.narration: Amazing! 10 protons creates neon, the noble gas that glows brilliantly when electricity passes through it!

challenges.instruction: Look at the nucleus with 6 protons and 6 neutrons. What element have you built?
challenges.hint: Check the atomic number on the periodic table for 6 protons.
challenges.narration: Spot on! 6 protons makes carbon, the foundational element of all known life on Earth.

challenges.instruction: Fill the electron shells for neon. Remember, the first shell holds up to 2 electrons, and the second shell holds up to 8.
challenges.hint: Put 2 electrons in the innermost shell, then place the remaining 8 in the second shell.
challenges.narration: See how its outer valence shell is completely full? That stable electron configuration is why neon doesn't easily react with other chemicals!

challenges.instruction: Start with a sodium atom (11 protons) and remove one electron to create a sodium ion with a positive charge.
challenges.hint: Sodium has 11 electrons when neutral. Take one away so you have 10 left.
challenges.narration: You removed an electron and created a sodium ion! This positive cation is half of the table salt dissolved in your soup.

challenges.instruction: Build carbon-14, a radioactive isotope of carbon used by scientists to date ancient fossils.
challenges.hint: Carbon always has 6 protons, but carbon-14 has two extra neutrons compared to standard carbon-12.
challenges.narration: Brilliant! You built carbon-14, demonstrating how isotopes share the same atomic number but differ in mass number due to extra neutrons.

data.imagePrompt: Vibrant and colorful neon signs glowing brightly in a bustling modern city street at night
